problem: _ref.allocate at line 17 reads weights to the end, so a generator or iterator leaves nothing for line 19 and allocate silently returns [] (e.g. allocate("10.00", (w for w in [1,2,3])) -> [] instead of [1.67, 3.33, 5.00]).

Converting amount and shares to float loses precision beyond about 2^53 units, so the shares no longer add up to the amount and money is lost or created (allocate("12345678901234567.89", [1,1]) loses 0.21; a negative leftover can also over-allocate).

Decimal weights that pass validation overflow to inf or underflow to 0.0 in float(w), crashing with ValueError (NaN) or ZeroDivisionError where the reference succeeds (e.g. weights ["1e400", 1] or ["1e-400"]*2).

Float remainders break the largest-remainder, lowest-index tie-break, so leftover units go to the wrong share even for ordinary amounts (allocate("1.68", ["3","0.7","1.1"]) -> [1.05, 0.24, 0.39] vs reference [1.05, 0.25, 0.38]).

Production code imports reference_impl and runs the whole exact allocation only for validation, then discards the result, doubling the work per call and tying production behaviour to the reference module.
